title: Heterogeneous Cohort A/B Controller and Auto-Rollback Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We need an experiment controller that safely runs A/B and canary rollouts across heterogeneous traffic slices (by tenant, region, device class) with automated rollback and shadowing capabilities. Current rollout tooling is conservative and manual: engineers assemble ad-hoc configs, monitoring, and separate scripts for rollback. This increases TTR and risk for regression.
background_and_context: Teams are increasingly deploying model variants frequently (weekly) and need low-friction experiments that meet SLAs. Existing experiments focus on flat exposure or static cohots; they lack per-cohort sensitivity control, hierarchical statistical checks, and integration with automatic fallback policies in the runtime. This project ties model lifecycle controls (exposure, scheduling, safety checks) to the Console and Serving runtime so rollouts become observable and reversible with short TTR.
goals: 1) Provide a controller that can allocate traffic heterogeneously across cohorts and adjust exposure dynamically.
goals_2: 2) Implement multi-metric sequential statistical checks with configurable alpha-spending and power targets.
goals_3: 3) Support shadow traffic and fast auto-rollback triggers with clear playbooks for manual override.
proposal_summary:
Build "CohortConductor": a controller service + Console UI that manages staged A/B experiments. Key features:
- Hierarchical cohort allocator: supports nested cohorts (global -> region -> tenant) and proportional/fixed exposure.
- Exposure thermostat: dynamic exposure increases conditioned on safety signals and metric convergence.
- Sequential statistical engine: supports both frequentist (alpha spending, O'Brien-Fleming) and Bayesian (Bayes factor/credible intervals) checks, pluggable per-experiment.
- Multi-metric decision policy: primary metric(s) with guard rails on secondary metrics (latency, error, cost).
- Shadow runner: duplicate traffic to variants for offline signal collection.
- Auto-rollback policy: immediate or staged rollback when thresholds hit, with an audit trail and human-in-the-loop override.
- Integration with Redwood Console for visualization, and with serving runtime for fast fallback and variant routing.
detailed_design_notes:
Architecture:
- CohortConductor (control-plane): REST/control API; experiment spec store; scheduler; sequential-test engine; event logger to audit log store.
- Runtime hooks: lightweight SDK in serving runtime to fetch routing table and observe fallback decisions; fast path for emergency rollbacks.
- Console UI: experiment canvas to define cohorts, exposure schedules, metrics, and rollback policies.
- Metrics plumbing: tie to existing observability pipeline (traces, per-route token costs, latency histograms).
Decision points:
- Default statistical engine: start with alpha-spending O'Brien-Fleming for P0 experiments, and Bayes for longer-running continuous tests.
- Exposure ramp: default 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows, gated by signal pass/fail.
- Rollback granularity: allow per-cohort rollback vs. full experiment revert.
acceptance_criteria: Product: Console UI lets PM/Eng author an experiment with nested cohorts and set multi-metric policies.
Engineering: CohortConductor can execute a staged rollout on a canary cluster and follow the exposure schedule without manual scripts.
Safety: Sequential engine correctly flags a failing trial and triggers the auto-rollback path in the runtime within SLO (<= 5 minutes).
Observability: Dashboard shows cohort-level metrics (primary/secondary), exposure history, and a clickable audit trail for rollback events.
Docs: Runbook and playbook published with one-click manual override and post-mortem checklist.

metrics_and_success_criteria: Primary success: reduce manual rollback latency from current average to <5 minutes for automated cases, and reduce time-to-ship for safe model changes by 30% for pilot teams. Secondary: fewer post-release regressions as measured by user-facing error rate and quality deltas on held-out prompts.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Cohort-level guard alerts when secondary metrics exceed thresholds.
- Auto-rollback event alerts to on-call with summary of triggers.
- Experiment health score in Console with green/amber/red thresholds.
- Tracing link to request examples that hit the variant and produced anomalous outputs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (pilot): internal infra team only, run 10 experiments across three services using fixed 5% canaries (4 weeks).
Phase 1: widen to 3 external pilot customers with SSO and audit logs (6 weeks).
Phase 2: general availability, add advanced scheduling and Bayesian engine (Q3 release).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false-positive rollbacks on noisy metrics. Mitigation: require persistent signals (sustained window) and cross-metric confirmation before auto-rollback. Risk: complexity for users. Mitigation: provide sensible defaults and curated templates for common rollout patterns.
playbook_high_level:
- When an auto-rollback fires, CohortConductor will revert routing instantly for affected cohorts, mark experiment as 'Rolled back', and create an audit event.
- On-call review: validate telemetry, snapshot the failing requests, and open a post-mortem ticket if customer-impacting.
- Manual restore flow: require annotated justification and a cooldown window before re-run.
